- If sentiment turns positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.0) or shows strong bearish momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops after rising) and sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, model often holds too high; adjust downward by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 consecutive days, apply downward bias correction (−1–2% per day) until price stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “1.0” (strong bullish) followed by true price drop, model overreacts; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 7–14 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend (e.g., >3% drop/day) and model holds steady or rises, apply downward correction (−2–5% per day) for next 5–10 days.  
- If model forecast is below true outcome for 3+ days, model may be underestimating volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment history shows “0.0” for 3+ days, model tends to be flat or slightly overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply downward correction (−2–5%) for next 3–7 days.
